name: LegalBrain-Indic-Legal-Corpus
description: A large-scale Indian legal dataset of context-question-answer triples derived from publicly accessible Indian legal materials (court judgments, law commission reports, government acts and notifications). Curated for grounded legal question answering, supervised fine-tuning, retrieval-augmented generation, and legal NLP evaluation. The released split is predominantly English (Latin script), with limited Devanagari (Hindi) content; broader Indic-language coverage is a documented limitation rather than a benchmark capability.
dataCollection: The dataset was assembled from publicly accessible Indian legal web sources collected between 2024 and 2025: Supreme Court of India judgment portal (main.sci.gov.in), selected High Court judgment repositories, India Code legislative portal (indiacode.nic.in), e-Gazette of India (egazette.nic.in), and Law Commission of India reports (lawcommissionofindia.nic.in). No proprietary legal databases were used. Raw HTML and PDF documents were processed through URL extraction, HTML stripping, PDF OCR (Tesseract 5.x), text normalisation, near-duplicate removal via MinHash LSH (Jaccard 0.85) plus exact context-fingerprint deduplication over normalised first-180-token prefixes, length filtering, legal-keyword filtering, and PII keyword scanning. Context-question-answer triples were generated from raw legal passages using meta-llama/Llama-3.1-8B-Instruct via the Groq API with a fixed prompt template. A stratified subset of generated triples was reviewed by two volunteer reviewers using the Argilla annotation platform; inter-rater Cohen kappa on a 200-triple dual-review overlap set was 0.68 for grounding and 0.71 for answer support. The reviewer effort focused on quality-flagged candidates surfaced by the automated pipeline rather than a uniform random sample of the 6.06M-row corpus; the bulk of the corpus passed automated quality filters only. Reference answers should be treated as supervised-learning targets and not as authoritative legal interpretations.
rai:dataBiases: The corpus overrepresents higher-court (Supreme Court, High Court) English-language judgments relative to district-court, tribunal, and vernacular-language legal practice. The released sample is empirically 99.5% English/Latin-script; broader Indic-language coverage is a documented limitation. Reference answers were generated by Llama-3.1-8B-Instruct, which introduces model-specific surface style: token-overlap metrics (Token F1, ROUGE-L) may structurally favour Llama-family evaluation models whose output resembles the reference generator. The lexical grounding score is structurally elevated for reference answers by construction. The corpus reflects the pre-July-2024 Indian statutory framework and does not cover the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita (BNS), Bharatiya Nagarik Suraksha Sanhita (BNSS), or Bharatiya Sakshya Adhiniyam (BSA). Legal precedents may embed historical judicial biases on gender, caste, and socioeconomic status that are present in the source materials.
rai:dataLimitations: This dataset must not be used to provide legal advice without qualified human review. It does not support claims about legal correctness, real-litigant outcome prediction, post-July-2024 statutory reasoning, multilingual Indic legal capability (beyond limited English/Hindi), or fitness for unsupervised legal advice. The grounding score is not a proof of legal correctness or semantic entailment. The benchmark split is not temporally or source-stratified; evaluation numbers measure in-distribution performance, not generalisation to unseen legal sources. A within-dataset 8-gram Jaccard contamination screen found 0.8% flagged pairs (4/500), which are template variants rather than leaks. Contamination against LLM pretraining data cannot be ruled out.
rai:dataUseCases: Intended uses: (1) reproducible benchmarking of retrieval and retrieval-augmented generation systems on Indian legal text; (2) supervised fine-tuning of legal QA models on English-language Indian legal context-question-answer triples; (3) evaluation of NLI faithfulness, grounding, and citation-extraction capabilities on Indian legal vocabulary; (4) academic research on Indian legal NLP. Not intended for: deployment in real legal proceedings, provision of legal advice, profiling of litigants, re-identification of protected persons (POCSO, minors, victims), or any use that affects legal rights without human oversight.
rai:dataSocialImpact: Potential positive impacts: improves reproducible evaluation infrastructure for Indian legal AI research; lowers barriers to developing legal QA tools that could improve access-to-justice for underserved populations. Potential negative impacts: misuse as a sole source of legal advice by non-experts could cause harm; models trained on this corpus may hallucinate plausible-sounding but legally incorrect information; uneven source coverage could amplify existing inequities in how different courts or legal areas are represented in AI systems; privacy risks remain from party names and case details in source judgments.
rai:personalSensitiveInformation: The dataset is derived from publicly accessible Indian court judgments and government documents. It may contain names of parties, witnesses, and other identified persons in their legal roles. Cases requiring mandatory victim-identity protection (POCSO Act, sexual-offence proceedings, juvenile cases) were excluded at collection time. A PII keyword audit found 4.2% of evaluation rows and 4.71% of corpus rows contain sensitive keyword matches (predominantly abstract legal references where victim identity is already anonymised in the source text); no Aadhaar UIDs were detected. Downstream users are responsible for additional redaction or purpose-limitation assessment under India's Digital Personal Data Protection Act 2023 before deployment.
wasDerivedFrom: Publicly accessible Indian court judgment repositories, law commission publications, and government legislative portals. No proprietary or licensed databases were used.

wasGeneratedBy.dataCollection: Automated crawling of publicly accessible Indian legal web sources, followed by HTML and boilerplate stripping. OCR applied to scanned PDFs using Tesseract 5.x with regex-based normalization of section markers, citations, and case line references. Language detection and segmentation using spaCy and Indic NLP Library. Near-duplicate removal via MinHash LSH (Jaccard threshold 0.85) and exact-context-fingerprint deduplication over normalized first-180-token prefixes.
wasGeneratedBy.dataAnnotation: Context-question-answer triples generated by a large language model prompting pipeline (meta-llama/Llama-3.1-8B-Instruct via Groq API) to produce candidate QA pairs. A stratified subset of quality-flagged candidates was loaded into Argilla for human review by two volunteer reviewers; hallucinations were corrected, citation grounding improved, and unsupported answers rejected in this reviewed subset. The bulk of the 6.06M-row corpus passed automated quality filters (deduplication, length, legal-signal, script, PII) only and was not individually human-reviewed. Reviewers were not credentialed legal practitioners. Collection period: 2024-2025.
